title: Asynchronous Usage with binance
text: Synchronous HTTP blocks R session waiting reply. Asynchronous mode lets fire multiple requests process results arrive – useful bots poll several endpoints place orders parallel.

title: Asynchronous Usage with binance
text: Event loop: R built-event loop like Node.js Python’s asyncio. Promises resolve event loop ticks via later::run_now(). scripts vignettes, drain loop (!loop_empty()) run_now(). Shiny apps event loop runs automatically.
code: box::use(   binance[BinanceMarketData, BinanceTrading, BinanceAccount, get_api_keys],   coro[async, await],   later[run_now, loop_empty],   promises[then, catch, promise_all] )

title: Asynchronous Usage with binance
text: Pass async = TRUE class constructor. Methods return promises instead data.tables: Key pattern: define async function, await API call, return result. Drain event loop (!loop_empty()) run_now().
code: market <- BinanceMarketData$new(async = TRUE)  get_ticker <- coro::async(function() {   ticker <- await(market$get_ticker(symbol = "BTCUSDT"))   return(ticker) })  get_ticker() while (!later::loop_empty()) {   later::run_now() }

title: Asynchronous Usage with binance
text: Chain several awaited calls sequence – one resolves next begins:
code: market <- BinanceMarketData$new(async = TRUE) results <- NULL  fetch_tickers <- coro::async(function() {   btc <- await(market$get_ticker(symbol = "BTCUSDT"))   eth <- await(market$get_ticker(symbol = "ETHUSDT"))   results <<- list(btc = btc, eth = eth)   return(invisible(NULL)) })  fetch_tickers() while (!later::loop_empty()) {   later::run_now() } results$btc results$eth

title: Asynchronous Usage with binance
text: requests independent, fire simultaneously collect results – async equivalent Promise.() JavaScript:
code: market <- BinanceMarketData$new(async = TRUE) results <- NULL  fetch_parallel <- coro::async(function() {   # Launch both requests concurrently (no await yet)   btc_promise <- market$get_ticker(symbol = "BTCUSDT")   eth_promise <- market$get_ticker(symbol = "ETHUSDT")    # Await them together   res <- await(promises::promise_all(btc = btc_promise, eth = eth_promise))   results <<- res   return(invisible(NULL)) })  fetch_parallel() while (!later::loop_empty()) {   later::run_now() } results$btc results$eth

title: Asynchronous Usage with binance
text: prefer promise-pipeline style, use catch:
code: market <- BinanceMarketData$new(async = TRUE) chain_result <- NULL  market$get_24hr_stats(symbol = "BTCUSDT") |>   promises::then(function(stats) {     chain_result <<- stats     return(invisible(NULL))   }) |>   promises::catch(function(err) {     message("Error: ", conditionMessage(err))     return(invisible(NULL))   })  while (!later::loop_empty()) {   later::run_now() } chain_result

what: Practical Example: Fetching Multiple Symbols Concurrently
title: Asynchronous Usage with binance
text: common use case polling price data watchlist symbols. async mode, requests fly parallel rather sequentially:
code: market <- BinanceMarketData$new(async = TRUE) symbols <- c("BTCUSDT", "ETHUSDT", "SOLUSDT", "BNBUSDT") all_tickers <- NULL  fetch_watchlist <- coro::async(function() {   # Fire all requests concurrently   ticker_promises <- lapply(symbols, function(sym) {     return(market$get_ticker(symbol = sym))   })   names(ticker_promises) <- symbols    # Await all at once   res <- await(do.call(promises::promise_all, ticker_promises))   all_tickers <<- res   return(invisible(NULL)) })  fetch_watchlist() while (!later::loop_empty()) {   later::run_now() }  # Each element is a data.table with the ticker result all_tickers$BTCUSDT all_tickers$ETHUSDT

title: Asynchronous Usage with binance
text: critical piece async R event loop. Promises resolve event loop ticks. interactive session Shiny app, event loop runs automatically. scripts vignettes, must drive manually. timeout guard: Shiny applications, event loop managed – simply return promises reactive expressions Shiny handles resolution.
code: # Idiomatic event loop drain while (!later::loop_empty()) {   later::run_now() } deadline <- Sys.time() + 30  # 30-second timeout while (!later::loop_empty() && Sys.time() < deadline) {   later::run_now(timeoutSecs = 0.1) }

title: Asynchronous Usage with binance
text: Inside async functions, use tryCatch around await calls structured error handling:
code: market <- BinanceMarketData$new(async = TRUE)  safe_fetch <- coro::async(function() {   result <- tryCatch(     await(market$get_ticker(symbol = "INVALIDPAIR")),     error = function(e) {       message("Caught error: ", conditionMessage(e))       return(NULL)     }   )   return(result) })  safe_fetch() while (!later::loop_empty()) {   later::run_now() }

text: Rule thumb: await() must appear RHS <- bare statement – never inside another expression.

title: Package Tour and Data-Shape Conventions
text: shape policy shared alpaca kucoin. guiding rule : Identify entity endpoint, return one row per entity. trade gets row. order gets row. asset balance gets row. funding-rate snapshot gets row. Anything nested entity becomes flat column row additional row different axis — never list column — data dropped; fields don’t fit per-entity row surfaced via sibling method attribute returned data.table. five shape treatments. handful endpoints use two treatments together nesting two layers.

what: Treatment E — JSON string for dynamic-key or array-of-array objects
title: Package Tour and Data-Shape Conventions
text: nested object dynamic keys (different products different key sets) array arrays inner grouping carries semantic meaning, neither ;-collapse wide-prefix preserves structure. Serialise whole field JSON string; recover jsonlite::fromJSON. used: spot exchangeInfo permission_sets, Earn get_flexible_products / get_flexible_position’s tier_annual_percentage_rate.
code: # spot exchangeInfo `permissionSets` is an array of arrays — each # inner array is an alternative permission set the user can satisfy. # `;`-joining would collapse `[["A","B"]]` and `[["A"],["B"]]` to # the same `"A;B"`, losing the grouping. info <- market$get_exchange_info("BTCUSDT") info$permission_sets #> [1] "[[\"SPOT\",\"MARGIN\",\"TRD_GRP_004\"]]" #> [2] NA  # Recover the structure jsonlite::fromJSON(info$permission_sets[1], simplifyVector = FALSE) #> [[1]] #> [[1]][[1]] #> [1] "SPOT" #>  #> [[1]][[2]] #> [1] "MARGIN" #>  #> [[1]][[3]] #> [1] "TRD_GRP_004" # Earn `tierAnnualPercentageRate` has dynamic keys per product # (different size tiers). products <- earn$get_flexible_products(asset = "USDT") products$tier_annual_percentage_rate #> [1] "{\"0-5BTC\":0.05,\"5-10BTC\":0.03}"  tiers <- jsonlite::fromJSON(products$tier_annual_percentage_rate[1]) tiers #> $`0-5BTC` #> [1] 0.05 #>  #> $`5-10BTC` #> [1] 0.03

text: need 1000 candles, pass fetch_all = TRUE. method pages forward range — following data stopping first empty short page — returns combined result. Binance returns candles first one startTime, empty leading stretch (e.g. dates symbol listed) skipped single request rather probed piece piece: Note: Large date ranges consume multiple API requests. title: Getting Started with binance
text: large pulls may want hold whole result memory. Pass on_page callback (used fetch_all = TRUE) page handed fetched — nothing accumulated, method returns invisibly, callback owns data (write disk, append database, ): exactly binance_backfill_klines() writes disk page page, interrupted download loses one page.
code: pages <- 0L candles <- 0L  market$get_klines(   symbol = "BTCUSDT",   interval = "1h",   start_time = as.POSIXct("2024-01-01", tz = "UTC"),   end_time = as.POSIXct("2024-02-01", tz = "UTC"),   fetch_all = TRUE,   on_page = function(page) {     pages <<- pages + 1L     candles <<- candles + nrow(page)     # e.g. data.table::fwrite(page, "klines.csv", append = TRUE)     return(invisible(NULL))   } )  cat("streamed", pages, "page(s),", candles, "candle(s)\n") #> streamed 1 page(s), 3 candle(s)

what: Driving the event loop: two ways

text: class never owns loop — $(), $connect(), $depth() just register callbacks later return immediately. Something pump later callbacks fire (R always-loop like Node.js). two options.

what: 1. Drive the loop yourself — recommended when embedding
title: Live WebSocket Streams with binance
text: Register handlers, $connect() (non-blocking), pump later::run_now(): right approach client lives inside program already runs later loop — Shiny app, trading engine also drives REST promises, timers, components loop. don’t even write loop: just $connect(), host loop fires handlers alongside everything else. Driving loop also lets work tick, add tasks, set stop condition.
code: stream <- BinanceMarketStream$new() stream$on("message", function(msg) record(msg)) stream$depth("BTCUSDT", speed = "100ms") stream$connect() # non-blocking: wires up + starts connecting, returns immediately  while (!later::loop_empty()) later::run_now(0.1) # you own the loop

what: Recording the order book to disk
title: Live WebSocket Streams with binance

title: Live WebSocket Streams with binance
text: manage reconnection. unexpected disconnect client reconnects exponential backoff (plus jitter, can never trip Binance’s connection-rate limit), reconnects proactively 23 hours beat Binance’s 24-hour forced disconnect, re-subscribes every stream reconnecting. reconnects exhausted, $run() returns — external supervisor (cron + lock, container restart policy) can bring recorder back.
code: stream <- BinanceMarketStream$new(max_reconnects = 10) # then $run() returns; let the supervisor restart

title: Live WebSocket Streams with binance
text: Interrupt session (Ctrl-C), call stream$close() handler — stops auto-reconnect, cancels timers, closes socket, $run() returns.

title: API Wrapper to Binance Cryptocurrency Exchange
text: API responses returned data.table objects. package targets consistent “one entity = one row, list columns” shape, exact transformation endpoint-specific. See method’s @return block precise list columns per-endpoint behaviour. transformations parsers apply: snake_case column names - camelCase keys JSON response (e.g. insertTime, quoteQty) converted snake_case (insert_time, quote_qty). handful endpoints additionally rename clarity (e.g. nested objects wide-prefixed parent_child columns; collapsed array fields land plural form like permissions). Type coercion well-known columns - millisecond timestamps become POSIXct; selected nested numeric filters extracted flat lot_min_qty / price_tick_size / min_notional columns. Shape normalisation nested arrays objects, applied per endpoint: Arrays plain strings (e.g. orderTypes, permissions, allowedSelfTradePreventionModes) → collapsed one ;-separated character column. Recover via strsplit(x, ";", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]. Arrays objects fixed schema (e.g. order fills, account assets, OCO orderReports, sub-account spotSubUserAssetBtcVoList) → exploded long format parent fields replicated <child>_ prefix child columns. 1-indexed position column added order matters. Single nested objects fixed schema (e.g. account commissionRates, locked-earn detail / quota) → flattened wide parent_child columns. Nested objects dynamic keys (e.g. spot exchange-info permissionSets, flexible-earn tierAnnualPercentageRate) → serialised JSON string column inner structure preserved; recover via jsonlite::fromJSON(x). Endpoints reshape rather drop: parsers never discard API data — every field either row, sibling row, sibling method’s return, attached attribute returned data.table. get_account_info() (spot) - account-level fields returned single row; companion balances array parsed sibling get_balances() (methods hit /api/v3/account parse different halves). get_account() (futures) - one row per asset balance; companion positions array parsed sibling get_positions() (hits /fapi/v2/positionRisk). get_exchange_info() (spot futures) - one row per symbol. full per-symbol filters array preserved JSON-encoded filters_raw column alongside curated lot_* / price_* / min_notional columns (recover jsonlite::fromJSON(dt$filters_raw[1])). Exchange-wide blocks (rate limits, exchange-wide filter rules, futures margin-asset config) exposed via sibling methods class: get_rate_limits(), get_exchange_filters(), (futures ) get_futures_assets(). serverTime long-standing get_server_time(). constants (timezone = "UTC", futuresType = "U_M") re-exposed. OCO endpoints (add_oco_order(), cancel_oco_order()) expand richer orderReports payload; thinner orders duplicate strict subset data omitted. Klines special case: Binance returns positional arrays instead named objects, assign descriptive column names (open_time, open, high, low, close, volume, close_time, etc.) matching Binance documentation. column expect missing, check method’s @return; still looks wrong, please file issue.

what: BinanceBase: Abstract Base Class for Binance API Clients — BinanceBase
title: BinanceBase: Abstract Base Class for Binance API Clients — BinanceBase
text: Provides shared infrastructure Binance R6 classes, including API credential management, sync/async execution mode, timestamp source configuration, standardised method calling implementation functions.

title: BinanceBase: Abstract Base Class for Binance API Clients — BinanceBase
text: class thin Binance specialisation connectcore::RestClient, shared transport base. request funnel, sync/async branching, retry, throttle live connectcore; BinanceBase supplies two venue-specific seams — Binance authenticates request (.sign(), delegating connectcore::hmac_query_sign() X-MBX-APIKEY header) reports error (.parse_envelope(), honours Binance's negative-code error body). Binance carries signed parameters query string, body configured body_format = "query".

title: BinanceBase: Abstract Base Class for Binance API Clients — BinanceBase
text: async parameter controls execution mode API methods: async = FALSE (default): methods return results directly (data.table, character, etc.). async = TRUE: methods return promises::promise objects resolve types. async, use coro::async() await() promises::() consume results. promises package must installed async mode (Suggests dependency).

title: BinanceBase: Abstract Base Class for Binance API Clients — BinanceBase
text: time_source parameter controls clock used HMAC request signing: "local" (default): uses local UTC clock. "server": fetches Binance server time via GET /api/v3/time authenticated request. slower (one extra HTTP round trip) ensures signing works even local clock sync.

Columns: fee_tier (integer) Commission fee tier. can_trade (logical) Whether trading permitted. can_deposit (logical) Whether deposits permitted. can_withdraw (logical) Whether withdrawals permitted. total_initial_margin (character) Total initial margin required. total_maint_margin (character) Total maintenance margin required. total_wallet_balance (character) Total wallet balance. total_unrealized_profit (character) Total unrealised PnL. total_margin_balance (character) Total margin balance. total_cross_wallet_balance (character) Total cross-wallet balance. available_balance (character) Available balance new positions. max_withdraw_amount (character) Maximum withdrawable amount. asset_asset (character) Per-asset symbol — one row per asset (Binance returns symbol asset field within assets array, hence doubled name asset_ prefixing). asset_wallet_balance (character) Per-asset wallet balance. asset_unrealized_profit (character) Per-asset unrealised PnL. asset_margin_balance (character) Per-asset margin balance. asset_available_balance (character) Per-asset available balance. Account-level fields replicated asset row. per-position data (entry price, leverage, side, unrealised PnL open contracts) use get_positions() — Binance returns positions alongside assets response, heterogeneous shape (one entity asset balance, derivative position) combining require Cartesian join user expects. therefore intentionally drop positions array ; get_positions() hits /fapi/v2/positionRisk returns one row per open position.

text: (data.table | promise<data.table>) one row per symbol, symbol fields returned API, converted snake_case (empty Binance returns symbols). Key columns include: symbol (character) Trading pair identifier (e.g., "BTCUSDT"). pair (character) Underlying pair. contract_type (character) Contract type (e.g., "PERPETUAL"). status (character) Trading status ("TRADING", etc.). base_asset (character) Base asset code (e.g., "BTC"). quote_asset (character) Quote asset code (e.g., "USDT"). margin_asset (character) Margin asset code (e.g., "USDT"). price_precision (integer) Decimal precision prices. quantity_precision (integer) Decimal precision quantities. order_types (character) Semicolon-separated allowed order types. Recover via strsplit(dt$order_types[1], ";", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]. time_in_force (character) Semicolon-separated allowed time--force values. underlying_sub_type (character | NA) Semicolon-separated underlying sub-types (NA symbol omits field, many non-coin / index-style contracts ). permission_sets (character | NA) Semicolon-separated permission sets (NA symbol omits field). lot_min_qty (numeric | NA) Minimum order quantity (LOT_SIZE filter; NA symbol carries LOT_SIZE filter). lot_max_qty (numeric | NA) Maximum order quantity (LOT_SIZE filter). lot_step_size (numeric | NA) Quantity step size (LOT_SIZE filter). price_min (numeric | NA) Minimum price (PRICE_FILTER; NA symbol carries PRICE_FILTER). price_max (numeric | NA) Maximum price (PRICE_FILTER; NA symbol carries PRICE_FILTER). price_tick_size (numeric | NA) Price tick size (PRICE_FILTER; NA symbol carries PRICE_FILTER). min_notional (numeric | NA) Minimum notional value (MIN_NOTIONAL filter; NA symbol carries MIN_NOTIONAL filter). filters_raw (character | NA) JSON-encoded copy full per-symbol filters array. Preserves filter types pulled curated columns (PERCENT_PRICE, MARKET_LOT_SIZE, MAX_NUM_ORDERS, MAX_NUM_ALGO_ORDERS, MIN_NOTIONAL's extra fields, ...). Recover jsonlite::fromJSON(dt$filters_raw[1]). NA Binance returned filters symbol. Exchange-wide metadata returned endpoint exposed via sibling methods: get_rate_limits(), get_exchange_filters(), get_futures_assets(). Server time available via BinanceMarketData$get_server_time().

title: BinanceMargin: Margin Trading Operations — BinanceMargin
text: Provides methods margin borrowing, repaying, order management, account queries Binance. Inherits BinanceBase.

title: BinanceMargin: Margin Trading Operations — BinanceMargin
text: Borrowing / Repaying: Borrow repay assets cross isolated margin. Order Management: Place, cancel, query margin orders. Account Info: Query margin account details, max borrowable/transferable amounts. History: Retrieve interest history, force liquidation records, trade history. Isolated Margin: Query isolated margin accounts initiate isolated transfers.

title: BinanceMarketData: Spot Market Data Retrieval — BinanceMarketData
text: (data.table | promise<data.table>) one row per symbol, symbol fields returned API, converted snake_case (empty Binance returns symbols). Key columns include: symbol (character) Trading pair identifier (e.g., "BTCUSDT"). status (character) Trading status ("TRADING", "HALT", "BREAK"). base_asset (character) Base asset code (e.g., "BTC"). base_asset_precision (integer) Decimal precision base asset quantities. quote_asset (character) Quote asset code (e.g., "USDT"). quote_asset_precision (integer) Decimal precision quote asset quantities. quote_precision (integer) Decimal precision quote asset prices. order_types (character) Semicolon-separated allowed order types (e.g., "LIMIT;MARKET"). Recover vector via strsplit(dt$order_types[1], ";", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]. iceberg_allowed (logical) Whether iceberg orders allowed. oco_allowed (logical) Whether OCO orders allowed. oto_allowed (logical) Whether OTO orders allowed. quote_order_qty_market_allowed (logical) Whether quote quantity market orders allowed. allow_trailing_stop (logical) Whether trailing stop orders allowed. cancel_replace_allowed (logical) Whether cancel-replace allowed. is_spot_trading_allowed (logical) Whether spot trading enabled. is_margin_trading_allowed (logical) Whether margin trading enabled. lot_min_qty (numeric | NA) Minimum order quantity LOT_SIZE filter (NA symbol carries LOT_SIZE filter). lot_max_qty (numeric | NA) Maximum order quantity LOT_SIZE filter. lot_step_size (numeric | NA) Quantity step size LOT_SIZE filter. price_min (numeric | NA) Minimum price PRICE_FILTER (NA symbol carries PRICE_FILTER). price_max (numeric | NA) Maximum price PRICE_FILTER (NA symbol carries PRICE_FILTER). price_tick_size (numeric | NA) Price tick size PRICE_FILTER (NA symbol carries PRICE_FILTER). min_notional (numeric | NA) Minimum notional value MIN_NOTIONAL filter (NA symbol carries NOTIONAL filter). filters_raw (character | NA) JSON-encoded copy full per-symbol filters array. Preserves filter types pulled curated columns (PERCENT_PRICE, PERCENT_PRICE_BY_SIDE, MARKET_LOT_SIZE, MAX_NUM_ORDERS, MAX_NUM_ALGO_ORDERS, MAX_NUM_ICEBERG_ORDERS, ICEBERG_PARTS, MAX_POSITION, TRAILING_DELTA, ...). Recover jsonlite::fromJSON(dt$filters_raw[1]). NA Binance returned filters symbol. permissions (character | NA) Semicolon-separated trading permissions (e.g., "SPOT;MARGIN"). Recover via strsplit(dt$permissions[1], ";", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]. Note: newer symbols Binance often returns permissions = [] populates permission_sets instead, column NA symbols. Prefer permission_sets new code. permission_sets (character | NA) JSON string preserving Binance's array--arrays structure (e.g. '[["SPOT","MARGIN"],["TRD_GRP_004"]]'). Inner groupings carry semantic meaning — inner array alternative permission set — flatten ;. Recover jsonlite::fromJSON(dt$permission_sets[1]). NA symbol omits field. default_self_trade_prevention_mode (character) Default STP mode. allowed_self_trade_prevention_modes (character) Semicolon-separated allowed STP modes. Exchange-wide metadata returned endpoint (rateLimits, exchangeFilters, sors) exposed via sibling methods — see get_rate_limits() get_exchange_filters(). scalar serverTime available via existing get_server_time().

title: binance 0.8.0
text: connector’s 25 non-transport rlang::abort() sites — method’s argument parameter malformed violates rule request made (missing required order id, unset LIMIT price, bad ticker, recv_window cap) — now signal classed condition new abort_binance_validation_error() raiser, caller branches error type instead grepping message text. completes taxonomy: request funnel already raised typed transport conditions (0.7.0); covers input-validation surface. class vector c("binance_validation_error", "binance_error") (top rlang’s error classes). binance_error connector’s DOMAIN root, parallel transport connectcore_error root: validation failure transport failure, two roots never meet — exactly core_error / connectcore_error split fleet already uses. Catch binance_validation_error input bugs specifically, binance_error non-transport binance failure. message strings byte-identical bare rlang::abort() calls replaced (reverse-substitution proves every one 25 reproduces master exactly; golden tests pin representative site), existing tests downstream message greps keep matching. classes purely additive; conditionMessage() inherits(e, "error") unchanged. behaviour changes. Follows org convention (dereckscompany/tradebot-core#30; discussion “throw typed errors, bare strings”). transport/API funnel (abort_binance_error, rooted connectcore_error) untouched.

title: binance 0.7.0
text: failure surfaces request funnel (parse_binance_response()) now signal classed condition instead bare rlang::abort(), caller branches error type reads structured fields rather grepping message text. covers venue-code surface (negative code JSON body, can arrive even HTTP 200) plain non-2xx HTTP surface. class vector ordered specific -> general: binance_api_error_<status> (keyed HTTP status), binance_api_error (Binance failure), inherited connectcore family connectcore_api_error_<status> / connectcore_api_error / connectcore_error (HTTP transport failure fleet-wide). condition carries status (integer), code (Binance venue error code, NULL plain HTTP failure), url (query-string credentials redacted), body_snippet (response body) fields — read e$code, regex. message strings byte-identical previous "Binance API error <code>: <msg>" (venue-code path) "Binance HTTP error <status>\n<body>" (HTTP path), existing tests downstream message greps keep matching. classes fields purely additive. follows connector-subclass recipe documented connectcore 0.4.0 (?connectcore_conditions); floor bumped connectcore (>= 0.4.0).

title: binance 0.5.4
text: binance_backfill_klines() now retries transient request failures, single timeout longer truncates symbol’s history. Adds connectcore Imports.

title: binance 0.3.0
text: Live WebSocket market-data streams. new event-driven client Binance’s public spot streams, modelled Node.js ws API (Binance’s official connectors). Two new exported R6 classes: BinanceWsBase — abstract base: register handlers $("message"|"open"|"close"|"error", handler), $subscribe() / $unsubscribe(), $run() keep process alive pump R’s later event loop (, like Node, built libuv). Connection management automatic: full-jitter exponential-backoff reconnect unexpected close, proactive reconnect 23h (Binance’s 24h forced disconnect), automatic re-subscribe every tracked stream reconnect, library-handled ping/pong. BinanceMarketStream — typed spot streams; first endpoint $depth(symbol, speed), order-book diff stream (<symbol>@depth / @depth@100ms) — order-book data Binance archive, must captured live. Many symbols share one connection (1024 streams). Handlers receive raw JSON message string — parse jsonlite::fromJSON() write straight disk faithful archival. Unlike REST classes async flag: socket endless push stream single result, always event-driven (one thing R adds Node $run() keep loop alive). Built websocket later packages, now hard Imports. New vignette("websocket-streams", package = "binance") — event API, two ways drive event loop (later loop, $run()), order-book recorder pattern, reconnection. Typed contracts via roxyassert. new WebSocket classes adopt roxyassert: every @param/@return typed annotation, argument/return checks generated R/contracts-generated.R (committed, like NAMESPACE) documented contract runtime check come one source. first use roxyassert package; rest migrates incrementally (untyped tags untouched). Adds assert Imports.

title: binance 0.2.2

Return value now just file path; hidden state. Code previously read attr(result, "failures") capture warnings via withCallingHandlers() tryCatch() instead. NULL-input crashes three parsers. parse_orderbook, parse_paginated, add_order parser used dereference data$foo without guarding data = NULL, throwing "$ operator applied NULL" empty bodies JSON-parse failures. three now early-return empty data.table. collapse_string_array_fields NA-safe. scalar NA_character_ input throw (grepl → NA → (NA) → (NA) errors). paste(c("real", NA), collapse = ";") produce literal "real;NA". Fixed filtering NAs joining treating -NA vectors NA_character_. BinanceFutures::initialize() time_source = "server" branch returned wrong value. Used return assigned .get_timestamp_ms function instead invisible(self); branches now return invisible(self). One pre-existing test typo — test-live-integration-public.R called market$get_orderbook() (method doesn’t exist; get_depth()). Silently broken whenever BINANCE_LIVE_TESTS set.
